identity.title: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea: waking 1-3 h after sleep with dyspnea relieved by sitting/standing

technique.how: Ask whether the patient wakes from sleep, typically 1-3 hours after lying down, acutely short of breath and needing to sit up, stand or go to a window, with relief taking 15-30 minutes. Distinguish from nocturnal asthma/COPD (wheeze, cough, relieved by inhaler), GERD, sleep apnea and panic awakenings.
technique.prerequisites: Reliable history; ask the bed partner if available.

interpretation.positive_finding: PND indicates nocturnal redistribution of fluid into the pulmonary circulation with raised left-sided filling pressure; in ED dyspnea it is the most useful symptom for heart failure (LR+ 2.6) and is moderately specific (0.52-0.93 across studies).
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of PND does not exclude heart failure; sensitivity is poor (0.23-0.70) and many acute HF patients present without it.
interpretation.pitfalls: Nocturnal asthma, COPD, reflux-related bronchospasm and obstructive sleep apnea produce similar awakenings; patients may describe cough or wheeze rather than dyspnea (cardiac asthma).
interpretation.changes_what: PND raises probability of acute HF and justifies BNP/echo or POCUS; absence does not lower it enough to exclude HF.

sources.citation: Wang CS, FitzGerald JM, Schulzer M, Mak E, Ayas NT. Does this dyspneic patient in the emergency department have congestive heart failure? JAMA 2005;294(15):1944-56.
Signs and symptoms in adult patients with acute dyspnea: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Emerg Med 2018;25(1):3-11 (author list not retrievable via abstract tool; confirmed by PMID/DOI).
Mueller C, Frana B, Scholer A, Laule-Kilian K, Perruchoud AP. Emergency diagnosis of congestive heart failure: impact of signs and symptoms. Can J Cardiol 2005;21(11):921-4.

estimates.target_condition: Congestive heart failure as cause of dyspnea
estimates.population: Adult ED patients presenting with dyspnea; 22 studies pooled in RCE
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical/echo-based HF diagnosis per included studies
estimates.quote: the symptom of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (positive LR = 2.6; 95% CI, 1.5-4.5)

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of PND to exclude heart failure, or nocturnal dyspnea alone to diagnose it in a known asthmatic without other congestion signs.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Nightly PND with progressive orthopnea signals worsening decompensation and warrants urgent assessment for volume overload and ischemia.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: History-dependent; agreement depends on how the symptom is defined to the patient.

extraction_notes: Wang 2005 abstract provides LR+ 2.6 (1.5-4.5) for PND; the LR- (~0.70) is in the table only and not entered. The Eur J Emerg Med 2018 review reports only sensitivity/specificity ranges for PND (0.23-0.70; 0.52-0.93), so no pooled estimate is recorded from it. Mueller 2005 reports OR 2.4 for PND in ED dyspnea (an odds ratio, not an LR); cited for context only.
